"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 2560.

What it responds to, in plain terms:
  * The French/Italian preposition "de" / "d'" / "di" (English "of" / "from"), most strongly
    the elided "d" written before an apostrophe in French ("réglé d'après", "capable d'une").
    It is strongest when the surrounding words are French or Italian and weak in
    English, Spanish or Dutch, where "de" is an ordinary word.
  * The words for Germany and German (Germany, German, Deutsch, 德 in 德国, Đức), and the
    word "ethics" / "ethical" (also when split as "Eth" + "ic").
  * Weaker: European / Europe and a capital "De".
  * Slightly negative on the first token of every document, which has no context.
  * Strongly negative inside a long run (8+) of one repeated symbol, such as "········".

The program keeps a short look-back window inside the current document and reads only the
newest token, so it runs in one pass. Its values are rough magnitudes, not a fit: most of
the component's small, diffuse activations (about +/-0.1) are not described here.
"""

READS = ()

GERMAN = {
    "german", "germany", "deutsch", "deutsche", "deutschen", "deutschland",
    "德", "德国", "đức",
}
ETHICS = {"ethics", "ethical", "ethic", "ética", "éthique", "ethik", "ethically"}
FRENCH_ITALIAN = set(
    "le la les des du et une un est qui que dans pour sur au aux avec ce cette il elle "
    "sont été par ou mais della delle che per sono anche come gli nel nella "
    "di è à en se ne".split()
)
ENGLISH_SPANISH = set(
    "the and of is to with for in that it was are this be on as "
    "el los las y del con por una como".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids, docs = prefix.token_ids, prefix.document_ids
    doc = docs[-1]
    t = len(ids) - 1
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    # The first token of a document has no context and sits a little below zero.
    if t == 0 or docs[t - 1] != doc:
        return carry, -0.2

    # A long run of one repeated symbol (e.g. a row of middle dots) drives it negative.
    run = 0
    while run < 16 and t - run - 1 >= 0:
        if ids[t - run - 1] != ids[t] or docs[t - run - 1] != doc:
            break
        run += 1
    if run >= 8 and all(not c.isalnum() and not c.isspace() for c in raw):
        return carry, -2.0

    word = raw.strip().lower()
    if word in GERMAN:
        return carry, 4.0 if word == "德" else 2.5
    if word in ETHICS:
        return carry, 2.5
    if raw in (" European", " Europe", " europe", "欧洲", " De"):
        return carry, 0.5

    # French / Italian "de", "d" and "di" (of, from); the apostrophe after "d" is elided "d'".
    if raw in (" de", " d", " di", "de", "d", "'", "’"):
        window = [
            prefix.token_strings[i].strip().lower()
            for i in range(max(0, t - 12), t)
            if docs[i] == doc
        ]
        score = sum(w in FRENCH_ITALIAN for w in window) - sum(w in ENGLISH_SPANISH for w in window)
        french = score >= 2
        previous = prefix.token_strings[t - 1] if docs[t - 1] == doc else ""
        if raw in ("'", "’"):
            return carry, 1.0 if previous == " d" and french else 0.0
        if raw == " d":
            return carry, 1.0 if french else (0.5 if score >= 1 else 0.05)
        if raw == " di":
            return carry, 0.7
        return carry, 0.5 if french else 0.2
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2561, a weak document-start component.

Its activation is almost always near zero and has no clean concept behind it. The one
consistent feature is at the first token of each document (the packed row's document
boundaries, where attention is reset): there the activation is a fixed function of the
token alone, averaging about +0.09 with large spread (tokens like '#', 'package', 'The',
' to' are positive; '<|im_start|>', '\\n', '1', '#include' are negative). This program
predicts that average at every document start and 0 everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

START_MEAN = 0.094


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    is_start = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return None, (START_MEAN if is_start else 0.0)

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 2562: a "calendar-phrase and markup/SQL keyword" detector.

What it does, in plain terms. The component is usually near zero, with a small diffuse
background. It has large positive spikes in two kinds of text:

1. Relative calendar phrases: a month, weekday or season right after a relative cue such as
   "this", "next", "last", "every", "each", "following" ("this summer", "last Friday",
   "every April"), and, more weakly, a time unit after "next/every/each/following"
   ("next morning", "every week", "each year"). Calendar words in other places are
   slightly negative, and weekdays after "on" more so ("on Monday").
2. Structural keywords in code and markup: the SQL FROM of a SELECT query, the HTML tag
   names html/head/body/table/tr/details/figure/svg/form, written as "<table" or after
   "</" or "<", and LaTeX "\\begin{figure}" / "\\begin{table}" / "itemize" environment names.

Everything else is predicted as 0. Document starts get a tiny negative value, since the
first token of a document has its own offset.

The prediction is a set of hand-set values, not fitted weights: the values were chosen from
the mean activation in each class on training rows. Run it on any row with `data.predict`.
"""

READS = ()

CUES = {"this", "next", "last", "every", "each", "following", "coming", "that", "same", "past"}
MONTHS = {"January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August",
          "September", "October", "November", "December"}
WEEKDAYS = {"Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"}
SEASONS = {"spring", "summer", "fall", "autumn", "winter"}
CALENDAR = MONTHS | WEEKDAYS | SEASONS
TIME_UNITS = {"year", "month", "week", "weekend", "morning", "night", "day", "evening"}
MARKUP = {"html", "head", "body", "table", "thead", "tbody", "tr", "ul", "details", "figure",
          "svg", "form", "fieldset"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A new document in the packed row starts fresh: a small negative offset there.
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, -0.07
    strs = [s.strip() for s in prefix.token_strings]
    tok = strs[-1]
    prev = strs[-2].lower()

    # Calendar word after a relative cue ("this summer", "last Friday"); "on Monday" dips.
    if tok in CALENDAR:
        if prev in CUES and prev != "that":
            return None, 4.0
        if prev == "on":
            return None, -0.4
        return None, -0.2

    # Time unit after a forward-looking cue ("next morning", "every week").
    if tok in TIME_UNITS and prev in {"each", "every", "next", "following"}:
        return None, 1.0

    # Markup tag: "<table" as one token, or "table" after "<" or "</".
    if tok.lstrip("</").lower() in MARKUP and (tok[0] == "<" or prev in ("<", "</")):
        return None, 3.0

    # LaTeX environment names: \begin{figure}, \end{table}, \begin{itemize}.
    if tok in ("figure", "table") and prev == "{" and strs[-3] in ("begin", "end"):
        return None, 4.0
    if tok == "ize" and prev == "item":
        return None, 4.0

    # SQL FROM of a SELECT query (a SELECT within the last 25 tokens).
    if (tok == "FROM" or (tok == "from" and prev == "*")) and any(
        s.lower() == "select" for s in strs[-25:]
    ):
        return None, 4.0

    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2563: the "then / just / exactly" connective detector.

What it does: the component fires on Chinese connective adverbs that link one clause to
the next with the sense of "then, just, right after, exactly": 就 ("then", "just") and
便 ("then"), and the phrases built on them (就是 "is exactly", 就不, 就要, 就可以, 就会,
就能, 就在, 就像). It also fires, more weakly, on 即 and 遂 ("thereupon"), and on the
Thai particle ก็ ("then"). It stays near zero on the same characters inside ordinary
nouns and adjectives (成就, 方便, 便利, 便宜, 就业, 就医), which get small values here.

Why it works: the model reads Chinese as UTF-8 bytes, so 就 or 便 often arrives split over
two or three tokens. The activation lands on the token that completes the character, so
this program looks at the text decoded so far (text_prefixes) and not only at the
current token's own string.

Main logic: a word from a short list gets its typical strength. Otherwise, if the text now
ends with a connective character, it gets that character's strength. Otherwise, any token
still containing 就 or 便 gets 4.5. Everything else is 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Whole words: typical activation when the word is one token.
STRONG_WORDS = {
    "就是": 6.5, "就不": 6.5, "就是要": 7.5, "就要": 4.8, "就在": 4.0,
    "就可以": 3.7, "就能": 3.4, "就会": 3.3, "就像": 3.3,
}
# Words that contain 就 or 便 but are nouns, adjectives or "in order to": weaker.
WEAK_WORDS = {
    "成就": 2.0, "成就感": 0.0, "方便": 2.5, "便利": 1.0, "便捷": 0.5,
    "便宜": 0.2, "随便": 0.2, "就业": 0.1, "就医": 0.2, "也就是": 1.0,
    "也就是说": 0.7, "以便": 1.2, "即便": 1.5, "即可": 1.2,
}
# The character that completes a connective, and its strength on its own.
END_VALUE = {"就": 4.5, "便": 4.5, "即": 1.0, "遂": 1.5, "็": 4.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]
    if tok in STRONG_WORDS:
        return carry, STRONG_WORDS[tok]
    if tok in WEAK_WORDS:
        return carry, WEAK_WORDS[tok]
    if text and text[-1] in END_VALUE:
        return carry, END_VALUE[text[-1]]
    if "就" in tok or "便" in tok:
        return carry, 4.5
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2564 -- a "type definition starts here" detector.

What it does: the component is silent almost everywhere. It fires (negatively) on the keyword
that opens a type or class declaration in source code: `class`, `interface`, `struct`, `enum`,
`type`, `namespace`, `module`, `trait`, `impl`. The strength depends on what precedes the
keyword, because the same word is a declaration only in some places:

  * after an export or visibility modifier (`export interface`, `public class`, `pub struct`)
    it is strongest;
  * as the first word on its line (a top-level or indented declaration) it is strong;
  * after a closing brace, semicolon, bracket, backtick or line break (the end of a statement)
    it is weaker;
  * inside an object literal, argument list or expression (`type: "x"`, `f(class=...)`), or
    after a plain word in prose ("a type of wool"), it is zero.

Why: a type name is about to follow the keyword in these positions. This is a readable proxy
that predicts the activation from the surface text only; it is not the model's own circuit.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# how strongly each keyword opens a type definition, relative to `class`
KEYWORD_SCALE = {"class": 1.0, "interface": 1.4, "struct": 1.0, "enum": 0.9, "type": 0.6,
                 "namespace": 0.5, "module": 0.5, "trait": 0.4, "impl": 0.5}
MODIFIERS = {"export", "public", "private", "abstract", "static", "final", "pub", "partial",
             "sealed", "internal", "open"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word not in KEYWORD_SCALE:
        return carry, 0.0
    # the text of this document before the keyword (a new document starts a fresh context)
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    start = len(docs) - 1
    while start > 0 and docs[start - 1] == docs[-1]:
        start -= 1
    before = "".join(prefix.token_strings[start:-1])
    lines = re.split(r"\n|<\|[^|]*\|>", before)
    # inside an object literal, argument list or expression: not a declaration
    if before.rstrip().endswith(("{", ",", "[", "(", "=", ":")) and (
            not before.rstrip().endswith("{") or ":" in lines[-1]):
        return carry, 0.0
    stripped = before.rstrip(" \t\xa0")
    last = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_]+$", stripped)
    if last and last[0] in MODIFIERS:
        strength = 10.0 if last[0] == "export" else 8.0          # export/visibility modifier
    elif re.fullmatch(r"[\s\d+\-]*", lines[-1]):                     # first word on its line
        strength = 6.0
    elif stripped.endswith(("}", ";", "]", "\n", "`", "@@")) or not stripped:
        strength = 4.0                                            # after end of a statement
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, -strength * KEYWORD_SCALE[word]

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 2565: the digit 0 in decimal fractions and zero runs.

What it does, in plain terms: this component writes a strong signal when the token is a
"0" that sits inside a decimal fraction or a run of zeros, such as the 0 in 1.0, 0.00,
v0.1, E0042 or 0000. It is near zero on the 0 of an ordinary integer (10, 2000), and on
most other tokens. A few other digit-like pieces also fire: the 2 of an escaped UTF-8
byte (\\xe2, \\xc2) and a single-letter command-line flag after a dash (" - m").

Scored per token, with a run of zeros counted up to four:
  - "0" right after a nonzero digit (ordinary integer):          0
  - "0" right after "." (decimal point):  1.0 if the integer part
    is one digit (1.0, 0.00), else 0.5
  - "0" right after a token with letters (v0, E0042, A0):        0.65
  - "0" after other punctuation, a space or a document start:    0.15
  - each extra zero in the run adds 0.3; a run of four or more: 1.4
  - "2" right after "\\xe" or "\\xc":                             0.8
  - a single letter right after " -" or " --":                    0.4
  - everything else:                                            0

What it leaves out: most of the variance is small, diffuse activity (about ±0.07) on
ordinary letters and punctuation, which no simple rule here captures; and a few rare
large spikes (such as "{" after a JavaScript import). A lookup table of per-token
values would add a little more but would not be a concept.
"""
READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")
NONZERO_DIGITS = set("123456789")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    cur = toks[t]
    same = t > 0 and docs[t - 1] == docs[t]
    prev = toks[t - 1] if same else ""
    if cur == "2" and prev in ("\\xe", "\\xc"):
        return None, 0.8  # the 2 of an escaped UTF-8 byte, like \xe2
    if len(cur) == 1 and cur.isalpha() and prev in (" -", " --"):
        return None, 0.4  # a single-letter command-line flag, like "- m"
    if cur != "0":
        return None, 0.0
    run = 1  # zeros ending here, in this document, counted up to four
    j = t - 1
    while run < 4 and j >= 0 and toks[j] == "0" and docs[j] == docs[t]:
        run += 1
        j -= 1
    if run == 4:
        return None, 1.4  # a long run of zeros, as in 0000
    before = toks[j] if j >= 0 and docs[j] == docs[t] else ""
    if before in NONZERO_DIGITS:
        return None, 0.0  # the 0 of an ordinary integer, as in 10 or 2000
    if before == ".":
        # the 0 of a decimal fraction; strongest after a one-digit integer part, as in 1.0
        one_digit = j >= 1 and toks[j - 1] in DIGITS and not (j >= 2 and toks[j - 2] in DIGITS)
        base = 1.0 if one_digit else 0.5
    elif any(c.isalpha() for c in before):
        base = 0.65  # a zero glued to letters, as in v0.1 or E0042
    else:
        base = 0.15
    return None, base + 0.3 * (run - 1)

"""An unfinished copular predicate, especially its intervening modifiers.

Negation, scope words and sentence adverbs after 'be' are negative;
prospective verb phrases are positive. Degree/manner adverbs are weaker.
A short state carries the copula through modifiers, questions and common
adverbial idioms. Split words are joined, and documents reset the state.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
FINITE_BE = set('is are was were am isn aren wasn weren'.split())
FOREIGN_BE = set(('est sont était étaient sera serait suis sommes êtes '
                  'es son era eran soy somos está están '
                  'é são eram estão è sono erano '
                  'ist sind war waren bin был была было были будет').split())
CONTRACTIONS = {"'s", "'re", "'m", '’s', '’re', '’m'}
GROUPS = {
    'negation': set(('not n\'t \'t ’t nicht не').split()),
    'foreign_negation': set('pas jamais não'.split()),
    'no': {'no'},
    'additive': set(('also aussi auch également también também '
                     'anche также тоже').split()),
    'restrictive': set('only nur seulement apenas'.split()),
    'frequency': set(('often usually always never sometimes rarely ever once again '
                      'seldom typically generally frequently hardly '
                      'souvent toujours parfois siempre sempre immer oft всегда').split()),
    'continuation': set(('still already now just yet encore déjà noch schon bereits '
                         'jetzt ya aún todavía ahora já ainda agora '
                         'ancora già уже ещё еще').split()),
    'scope': set('all both each either neither'.split()),
    'discourse': set('then therefore thus hence indeed however nonetheless nevertheless'.split()),
    'stance': set(('actually really probably simply basically definitely certainly perhaps '
                   'seemingly apparently obviously undoubtedly evidently necessarily '
                   'presumably possibly truly plainly naturally somehow hereby').split()),
    'approximation': set('almost nearly exactly approximately'.split()),
    'intensity': set(('very extremely highly completely entirely fully '
                      'perfectly relatively').split()),
    'degree': set('so too much quite pretty rather somewhat'.split()),
    'past_time': set('previously originally initially formerly'.split()),
    'time': set('currently recently presently finally later first last soon today'.split()),
    'reflexive': set(('myself yourself himself herself itself ourselves yourselves '
                      'themselves oneself').split()),
    'prospective': set(('going gonna supposed suppose meant bound trying '
                        'beginning starting').split()),
    'focus': {'even'},
    'actuality': {'actually', 'really'},
    'coverage': set('mostly mainly primarily largely partly partially merely'.split()),
}
WORD_GROUP = {w: c for c, words in GROUPS.items() for w in words}
PASS_THROUGH = set(('of in at by for after to more most less than it this that '
                    'he she we they you there').split())
IDIOMS = {('of', 'course'), ('in', 'fact'), ('in', 'turn'), ('in', 'essence'),
          ('in', 'effect'), ('in', 'reality'), ('by', 'far'), ('no', 'longer'),
          ('at', 'all'), ('at', 'least'), ('at', 'best'), ('after', 'all'),
          ('for', 'sure'), ('more', 'than'), ('pretty', 'much')}

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def category(word):
    if word in WORD_GROUP:
        return WORD_GROUP[word]
    if word.isascii() and word.isalpha():
        pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
        if word.endswith('ly') and 'adverb' in pos:
            return 'ly_adverb'
        if pos == {'adverb'}:
            return 'adverb'
    elif word.isalpha() and word.endswith(('ment', 'mente')):
        return 'ly_adverb'
    return 'other'

# Ordinary value, then the additional response to a preceding copula.
VALUES = {
    'additive': (-0.055, -2.02),
    'adverb': (0.001, -0.033),
    'approximation': (-0.108, -1.226),
    'continuation': (-0.009, -1.913),
    'degree': (0.041, -0.611),
    'discourse': (0.043, -2.55),
    'focus': (0.044, -1.069),
    'foreign_negation': (-0.183, -1.119),
    'frequency': (0.079, -2.336),
    'idiom': (0.0, -3.4),
    'degree_idiom': (0.0, -1.1),
    'actuality': (-0.05, -2.4),
    'coverage': (0.0, -1.65),
    'intensity': (0.001, -0.18),
    'ly_adverb': (0.013, -0.891),
    'negation': (-0.097, -1.408),
    'no': (0.048, -0.802),
    'other': (-0.002, -0.014),
    'past_time': (-0.01, -1.986),
    'prospective': (-0.053, 0.943),
    'reflexive': (0.15, -3.8),
    'restrictive': (0.056, -1.418),
    'scope': (0.024, -1.796),
    'stance': (-0.051, -1.972),
    'time': (-0.008, -0.982),
}


def advance(carry, text, document):
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        carry = (document, '', '', 0., 0, '', 0.)
    _, previous, before, context, age, partial, word_context = carry
    raw = text.strip().lower()
    continuation = (partial and text and not text[0].isspace()
                    and raw.isalpha() and partial[-1:].isalpha())
    if continuation:
        word = partial + raw
        context = word_context
    else:
        word, word_context = raw, context
    cat = category(word)
    if ((previous, word) in IDIOMS
            or (previous == 'no' and before == 'by' and word == 'means')
            or (word == 'me' and previous == 'to' and before in {'seems', 'seem'})
            or (word == ',' and (previous in {'however', 'therefore', 'thus'}
                                or (previous == 'course' and before == 'of')))):
        cat = 'idiom'
        if (previous, word) in {('at', 'least'), ('at', 'best'),
                                ('by', 'far'), ('more', 'than')}:
            cat = 'degree_idiom'
    q = min(context, 1.2) if cat == 'prospective' else context
    base, slope = VALUES.get(cat, (0., 0.))
    value = base + slope * q
    if word in FINITE_BE or word in FOREIGN_BE:
        context, age = 1., 0
    elif raw in CONTRACTIONS:
        context, age = 1.2, 0
    elif word in {'be', 'been', 'being', 'être', 'ser', 'estar', 'essere', 'sein'}:
        context, age = .4, 0
    elif word in {'seems', 'seem', 'seemed'}:
        context, age = .8, 0
    elif age < 6 and (cat not in {'other', 'prospective'}
                     or word in PASS_THROUGH or not raw
                     or all(ch in ',\"“”' for ch in raw)):
        boost = 1.35 if cat in {'negation', 'frequency', 'stance', 'scope'} else 1.02
        context, age = min(2., context * boost), age + 1
    else:
        context, age = 0., 0
    return (document, word, previous, context, age, word, word_context), value, cat, q


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    carry, value, _, _ = advance(carry, prefix.token_strings[-1],
                                 prefix.document_ids[-1])
    return carry, float(value)

programs.haiku:
"""Matrix and array openers: layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2567 fires when the text opens a matrix,
an array, or a nested list literal.

What it does, in plain terms: it reads the text so far (the last 40 characters, restarting at
each document) and predicts a large value on the token that opens a matrix:

- 11 on the token that completes a LaTeX matrix environment name: "\\begin{pmatrix",
  "\\begin{bmatrix", "\\begin{vmatrix", "\\begin{smallmatrix" (the strongest case, the
  "atrix" or "matrix" token itself).
- 8 on "begin" right after "\\left[" or "\\left(" (a bracketed matrix such as
  "\\left[\\begin{array}").
- 3.3 on the matrix name in a closing "\\end{...matrix".
- 2.3 on the name "array", "cases" or "aligned" after "\\begin{".
- 1.5 on "\\begin" and "\\begin{" (any environment).
- 2.4 on "[[" that opens a 2-D list in code or math, such as "np.array([[" or "M = [[".
- 0.7 on "[" right after "=" (a list being assigned), and 0.4 on "([".

Everywhere else it predicts 0. The numbers are the mean activations measured on training rows
(e.g. the matrix name averages about 11, "[[" about 2.5). It does not model the small,
diffuse activity of ordinary tokens, which is about a quarter of the variance.
"""

import re

READS = ()

WINDOW = 40  # characters of recent text the rules look at

# (pattern on the recent text ending at the current token, predicted value), first match wins
RULES = [
    (re.compile(r"\\begin\{\w*(matrix|atrix)$"), 11.0),  # \begin{pmatrix, \begin{bmatrix
    (re.compile(r"\\left[\[(.]\\?begin$"), 8.0),  # \left[\begin, \left(\begin
    (re.compile(r"\\begin\{(array|cases|aligned)$"), 2.3),  # \begin{array}
    (re.compile(r"\\begin(\{)?$"), 1.5),  # \begin or \begin{
    (re.compile(r"(^|[\s(=,])\[\[$"), 2.4),  # [[ opening a 2-D list
    (re.compile(r"\\end\{\w*(matrix|atrix)$"), 3.3),  # \end{pmatrix
    (re.compile(r"=\s?\[$"), 0.7),  # x = [
    (re.compile(r"\(\[$"), 0.4),  # ([
]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (recent text, document id of the last token); the text restarts at each document

"""Approximate a language-sensitive word-ending response.

O/OS-ending word pieces usually get a negative response in Spanish,
Portuguese and Italian, but a positive adjustment in Romanian, Polish
and Czech. I/IS endings get a weaker Italian response. Whole words
are treated more conservatively. Word-frequency dictionaries supply
both lexical familiarity and a running estimate of the text's language.
Other tokens predict zero. This does not capture every activation.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('es', 'pt', 'it', 'ro', 'pl', 'cs', 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'nl', 'da')

@lru_cache(maxsize=65000)
def frequencies(word):
    return tuple(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in LANGUAGES)


def advance(word, scores, text):
    for chunk in re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+|[\W\d_]+', text.lower()):
        if chunk.isalpha():
            word = (word + chunk)[-80:]
        else:
            if len(word) > 1:
                values = frequencies(word)
                average = sum(values) / len(values)
                weight = min(1, len(word) / 5)
                scores = tuple(.9*a + weight*(b-average)
                               for a, b in zip(scores, values))
            word = ''
    return word, scores


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', (0.,) * len(LANGUAGES))
    _, stem, scores = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word, scores = advance(stem, scores, text)
    carry = (doc, word, scores)
    token = text.strip().lower()
    if not token.isalpha() or len(token) > 30:
        return carry, 0.
    o_ending = token.endswith(('o', 'os'))
    i_ending = token.endswith(('i', 'is'))
    if not (o_ending or i_ending):
        return carry, 0.

    piece = bool(stem) and not text.startswith((' ', '\n', '\t'))
    lexical = frequencies(stem + token if piece else token)
    romance_frequency = max(lexical[:3])
    other_frequency = max(lexical[3:])
    familiarity = max(0., romance_frequency - 2)
    contrast = max(-3., min(3., romance_frequency - other_frequency))
    probabilities = [math.exp((s-max(scores))/3) for s in scores]
    total = sum(probabilities)
    probabilities = [p/total for p in probabilities]
    romance = sum(probabilities[:3])
    east = sum(probabilities[3:6])
    french, italian = probabilities[7], probabilities[2]
    doubled = any(a == b and a not in 'aeiou'
                  for a, b in zip(token, token[1:]))
    vowels = min(3, sum(c in 'aeiou' for c in token))
    value = 0.
    if piece and o_ending:
        value = (-.15 - .085*familiarity - .034*contrast
                 - .10*(len(token) <= 2) - .07*token.endswith('s')
                 + .135*vowels - .53*romance + .66*east
                 + .29*french + .26*italian - .235*doubled)
    elif piece and i_ending:
        value = -.30*italian - .02*familiarity - .06*doubled
    elif o_ending and len(token) >= 3:
        # Whole-word responses exclude frequent English vocabulary.
        if romance_frequency > 3 and lexical[6] < 3.5:
            value = -.10 + .04*familiarity - .28*romance + .07*east
    return carry, float(value)

"""Romance word-ending fragments (layers.1.mlp.down_proj, component 2572).

The component goes negative on the last piece of a Spanish, Portuguese or Italian word when
that piece is a masculine-style ending: -os (strongest, e.g. "secret|os", "pas|os", "abus|os")
or -o ("pap|o", "cuat|ro" is similar), with -i weaker. It is near zero on whole words, on
English, and on most other text, and only slightly positive on a few non-Romance fragments.
Its size grows with how Romance the document looks so far.

The program keeps two counts per document: Romance function words (el, los, que, por, con,
uma, sono, ...) and English function words (the, and, of, ...). Romance share is
romance / (romance + english + 1). A piece with no leading space, made of lowercase letters,
gets:
  -0.9 * share^2 if it ends in -os,
  -0.5 * share^2 if it ends in -o,
  -0.3 * share^2 if it ends in -i,
  0 otherwise.
"""

READS = ()

ROMANCE_MARKERS = {" el", " los", " las", " que", " por", " para", " con", " una", " es",
                   " del", " il", " che", " della", " sono", " non", " não", " uma", " com",
                   " são", " dos", " muy", " pero", " como", " también", " este", " esta",
                   " cuando", " hay", " è", " questo", " anche", " molto", " gli", " nel",
                   " di", " da", " um", " do"}
ENGLISH_MARKERS = {" the", " and", " of", " is", " to", " that", " with", " for", " are",
                   " was", " you", " this", " it", " be", " on", " have", " from", " or",
                   " an", " by", " not"}


def is_fragment(token):
    """A mid-word piece: lowercase letters, no leading space."""
    return token.isalpha() and token.islower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (Romance markers, English markers) seen so far in this document
    new_doc = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    romance, english = (0, 0) if new_doc else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in ROMANCE_MARKERS:
        romance += 1
    elif token in ENGLISH_MARKERS:
        english += 1
    share = romance / (romance + english + 1)
    if not is_fragment(token):
        value = 0.0
    elif token.endswith("os"):
        value = -0.9 * share * share
    elif token.endswith("o"):
        value = -0.5 * share * share
    elif token.endswith("i"):
        value = -0.3 * share * share
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (romance, english), value

    environmental cultural'''.split())

    evangelical feminist nationalist socialist communist suffrage liberation
    independence conservation'''.split())

    marketing promotional sexual adult'''.split())

    'opt': 1.05, 'usr': .80, 'local': 1.10,

def word_info(word):
    forms = wordnet.base_forms(word, 'noun')
    base = min(forms, key=len) if forms else word
    return base, wordnet.parts_of_speech(word), wordnet.categories(word)


@lru_cache(None)
def modifier_info(word):
    base, pos, cats = word_info(word)
    adjective = 'adjective' in pos and word not in QUANTIFIERS
    noun = 'noun' in pos and word not in QUANTIFIERS
    relational = 'adj.pert' in cats

    word = token.strip().lower()

    if head in ASPECTS:

    if head in SOCIAL_HEADS and previous in SOCIAL_DOMAINS:

    if head in ('food', 'cuisine') and relational:

    if head in ('material', 'content') and previous in INFORMATIONAL:
        value += 1.24
    if head == 'guitar' and previous in ('electric', 'acoustic', 'bass'):
        value += .45
    if head == 'book':
        if modifier == 'child': value += 2.67
        if previous == 'comic': value -= 1.01
        if previous in ('picture', 'history', 'fantasy'): value += 1.51
    if head == 'music' and genre: value += .11
    if head == 'band' and genre: value += 1.90
    if head == 'novel': value += .46
    if head == 'song': value += .25
    if head == 'movement' and previous == 'independence': value += 2.70
    if head == 'school' and previous == 'high': value -= .57
    if head == 'room' and previous == 'emergency': value -= 1.89
    if head == 'team' and previous in (
        'sports', 'sport', 'rugby', 'football', 'management'
    ):
        value -= .45
    if head == 'day':
        if previous == 'modern': value -= 2.19
        if previous in ('christmas', 'thanksgiving', 'easter'): value -= 1.82
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    return (doc, (tail + token)[-80:]), value

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    before = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[-4:-1]]

    if tok == "out":
        return carry, OUT_AFTER.get(prev, -0.1)
    if tok in FULLWIDTH_SPEECH:
        return carry, FULLWIDTH_SPEECH[tok]
    speech_cue = any(b in COLONS or b in SPEECH_VERBS for b in before)
    if tok in QUOTE_VALUE and speech_cue:

What it does, in plain terms: it fires on the adjective that comes right after an
indefinite article, as in "a large", "a certain", "a better", "a new", "a good". There the
noun that the adjective modifies is still to come. The size of the response depends on the
adjective:
  - strongest on comparatives and a few words that open a phrase ("better", "larger",
    "more", "certain", "given", "specific", "particular", "different", "similar", "good", "new");
  - medium on size and extent words ("large", "big", "high", "long", "wide", "strong", ...);
  - weak on any other common adjective;
  - slightly negative on nouns and numbers that follow "a" but are not modifiers
    ("maximum", "public", "top", "two", ...).
"a" and "A" count fully; "an", "one", "any", "this", "very", "pretty", "really" count half.
Everything else is 0. Each document starts fresh, so the article must be in the same document.

exact adjective in ways the lists only partly capture, and it has a diffuse background
of small values that no short rule describes.

FULL_ARTICLES = {" a", " A", "A"}
HALF_CONTEXT = {" an", "An", " one", " any", " this", " very", " pretty", " really"}

HIGH = set("""
better larger higher lower longer shorter bigger greater smaller more less
certain given specific particular different similar good new
""".split())

MEDIUM = set("""
large big high long wide strong huge great small short significant considerable
single second healthy dark nice strange special unique fixed latter central
substantial comprehensive positive individual
""".split())

OTHER_ADJECTIVES = set("""
    abstract active actual additional advanced alternative another
    appropriate associated available average bad basic beautiful best
    black blue bright brown clean clear close cold common complete
    complex consistent constant correct critical current daily deep
    detailed determined difficult direct double dry dynamic early easy
    economic effective efficient electric empty entire equal even
    excellent existing external extra false fast federal final fine fit
    foreign former free fresh full fun future general global grand
    green growing happy hard heavy hot human ideal important impossible
    independent initial interesting internal international involved
    joint key kind known late leading legal light likely limited little
    live local lost low main major medical middle military
    minimal modern moving narrow national natural necessary
    negative normal odd official old open optional original overall
    parallel partial past perfect personal physical poor popular
    possible potential powerful present pretty previous primary prime
    private proper pure quick raw ready real recent red regular
    related relative relevant required rich right round safe same
    secret select separate simple social soft solid sound standard
    successful suitable super thick thin total traditional true typical
    unknown upper useful valid valuable variable various vertical warm
    white whole wrong young
""".split())

NOUNS_AND_NUMBERS = set("""
maximum minimum public top member two three four half self try type power multiple
""".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the last token of the prefix."""
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()

        gain = 1.0
    elif before in HALF_CONTEXT:
        gain = 0.5

        return carry, 0.0
    if word in HIGH:
        return carry, 2.0 * gain
    if word in MEDIUM:
        return carry, 1.0 * gain
    if word in OTHER_ADJECTIVES:
        return carry, 0.4 * gain
    if word in NOUNS_AND_NUMBERS:

    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2576 -- a "thinking out loud" detector.

This component goes negative inside a model's visible reasoning: passages of
self-doubt and step-by-step working ("Hmm", "Wait", "maybe", "Alternatively",
"Therefore", "Thus", "So", "Then"). It is most negative at the full stops,
paragraph breaks and connective words that start or end a reasoning step, and
it is close to zero in ordinary prose, encyclopaedic text, and code.

The program tracks how much of the current document is hedged, connective
reasoning: the number of reasoning markers seen so far, per 100 tokens, smoothed
at the start of each document and capped. It then multiplies that density by a
weight for the current token: 1 for a step boundary or connective, 0.6 for a
function word, 0.3 for another word, and 0 for digits and symbols. The predicted
activation is the negative of that product.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Words that signal hedging or backtracking in written reasoning.
MARKERS = {
    "wait", "hmm", "maybe", "perhaps", "alternatively", "therefore", "thus", "so",
    "then", "but", "since", "hence", "however", "probably", "yes", "actually",
    "mistake", "unsure",
}
# Words that start a new reasoning step.
CONNECTIVES = {
    "therefore", "thus", "so", "then", "but", "alternatively", "let", "hence",
    "since", "perhaps", "maybe",
}
FUNCTION_WORDS = set(
    "the a an is are was be it its this that in of to and or if can would could "
    "as with which".split()
)
BOUNDARY_MARKS = {".", "?", ":", ",", ")", "!", ";"}

SMOOTH = 50.0  # tokens added to the document length, so early density is not extreme
CAP = 5.0      # markers per 100 tokens, at most
SCALE = 0.25   # overall size of the predicted activation


def _word(token):
    return token.strip().strip(".,?!:;()\"'").lower()


def _weight(token):
    """How strongly this token reflects reasoning, from 0 to 1."""
    if "\n\n" in token or token.strip() in BOUNDARY_MARKS:
        return 1.0
    word = _word(token)
    if word in CONNECTIVES:
        return 1.0
    if re.search(r"\d|[^\w\s]", token):  # digits and symbols carry no reasoning
        return 0.0
    if word in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return 0.6
    return 0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry is (markers seen in this document, tokens in this document, document id)."""
    if carry is None:
        markers, n, last_doc = 0.0, 0, None
    else:
        markers, n, last_doc = carry
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:  # a new document starts: reset the count
        markers, n = 0.0, 0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    n += 1
    if _word(token) in MARKERS:
        markers += 1.0
    density = min(CAP, 100.0 * markers / (n + SMOOTH))
    return (markers, n, doc), -SCALE * density * _weight(token)

"""A small lexical/register approximation, plus boundary and phrase pulses.

WordNet feeling nouns receive a negative response. A short exponential memory
of common words, emotional verbs, group nouns, long words and digits supplies
a weaker register correction. Document openings receive a usually positive pulse,
adjusted for English frequency, capitals and numbers. Three fixed-expression
or metadata completions have separate negative pulses. Token-specific effects,
especially at document openings, are not reconstructed. Alphabetic token
fragments are looked up as words; split words are not assembled.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
# Ignore auxiliary 'does' (noun 'do') and pronoun 'who' (the WHO organization).
GRAMMATICAL = {'does', 'who'}


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def lexical(text):
    word = text.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    ascii_word = word.isascii() and word.isalpha()
    frequency = zipf_frequency(lower, 'en') if ascii_word else 0.0
    categories = (wordnet.categories(lower)
                  if ascii_word and len(word) > 2 and lower not in GRAMMATICAL
                  else ())
    common = frequency > 5
    feeling = 'noun.feeling' in categories
    # A score of the current token's contribution to the recent register.
    register = (-0.024 * common
                + 0.053 * (sum(c.isalpha() for c in word) > 8)
                + 0.017 * word.isdigit()
                + 0.044 * ('noun.group' in categories)
                - 0.082 * ('verb.emotion' in categories))
    local = -0.001 + 0.009 * common - 0.006 * word.islower() - 0.062 * feeling
    opening = (0.193 + 0.208 * frequency / 7
               - 0.222 * word.isupper() - 0.194 * word.isdigit())
    return local, register, opening


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    local, register, opening = lexical(text)
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        previous, before_previous, recent, tail = '', '', 0.0, 0.0
    else:
        _, previous, before_previous, recent, tail = carry
    value = local + recent + tail
    tail *= 0.45
    if first:
        value += opening
        if text == '<|endoftext|>':
            value = 2.07
        elif text == '<|im_start|>':
            value = -0.20
    else:
        word = text.strip().lower()
        if word == 'know' and previous.strip().lower() == 'never':
            value, tail = -0.69, -0.24
        elif word == 'reply' and previous.strip().lower() == 'latest':
            value = -0.81
        elif word == 'issue' and previous == '><' and before_previous == '_start':
            value = -1.08
    recent = 0.8 * recent + 0.2 * register
    return (doc, text, previous, recent, tail), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 2578: a document-start and old-verse detector.

In plain terms, this component writes almost nothing for most tokens. Its clearest effect is
on the first token of each document, where the model has no earlier text to lean on: there it
writes a positive value for words and sentence openers, and a negative one for digits,
punctuation-only tokens and special markup. Elsewhere it drifts slightly negative while the
document reads like archaic or poetic English (thee, thou, heart, soul, grace, ...), and stays
near zero in modern prose, code and non-English text. The drift is modelled as a decaying
share of such words over the current document, the carry being that share.
"""


READS = ()

# Archaic and poetic English words, which the component leans negative on.
ARCHAIC = set("thy thee thou thine doth hath dost art ere whence wherefore hither yonder oft alas ye".split())
POETIC = set(
    """love heart hearts soul souls joy grace beauty sweet hate hell fire flame honey wild evil
    enemies murder fear sorrow tears dream dreams sigh night death grave bones eyes mouth lips
    belly glad fun wonder sight glory woe heaven angel prey chains gates quiet thanks bliss""".split()
)
DECAY = 0.995  # how fast the running share forgets earlier words
DRIFT = -3.0  # size of the negative drift per unit of running share


def first_char_class(text):
    """'word', 'digit', 'special' (markup such as <|im_start|>) or 'punct' for a token's first character."""
    stripped = text.strip()
    if not stripped:
        return "space"
    c = stripped[0]
    if c.isalpha():
        return "word"
    if c.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if c == "<":
        return "special"
    return "punct"


DOC_START = {"word": 0.33, "space": 0.25, "punct": 0.23, "digit": -0.06, "special": -0.16}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    share = 0.0 if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    word = token.strip().lower()
    is_old = word in ARCHAIC or word in POETIC
    share = DECAY * share + (1 - DECAY) * float(is_old)
    if new_doc:
        return share, DOC_START[first_char_class(token)]
    return share, DRIFT * share

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, feature 2579: a parenthetical-connective detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
1. Parenthetical connectives. The component fires strongly and positively on a
   connective word that a writer drops into the middle of a sentence between commas:
   ", however,", ", respectively,", ", though,", ", too,", ", right?", ", meanwhile,".
   It also fires on fixed lead-in phrases: "of course", "in fact", "on the other hand",
   "for example", "for instance". Sentence-initial "However" is weak.
2. Terse text. Sentence-final periods are pushed negative in documents whose sentences
   often start in lowercase, such as photo captions, slide bullets, formulas and
   fragments. The program keeps a running average, over sentences, of how often a
   sentence starts with a lowercase word (reset at each document), and predicts a
   period's activation as a small negative multiple of that average.
Everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# connective -> typical activation when set off by a comma
COMMA_CONNECTIVES = {
    " however": 2.6, " respectively": 2.6, " meanwhile": 2.5, " unfortunately": 2.0,
    " too": 1.6, " though": 1.5, " moreover": 1.5, " right": 1.5, " anyway": 1.3,
    " depending": 1.2, " according": 1.1, " indeed": 1.1, " really": 1.0,
    " accordingly": 1.3, " naturally": 0.8, " nevertheless": 0.7, " obviously": 0.7,
    " admittedly": 0.7, " although": 0.5, " therefore": 0.5, " actually": 0.4,
    " alternatively": 0.5,
}
# (word before, connective) -> activation for fixed lead-in phrases
LEAD_INS = {
    (" of", " course"): 1.3,
    (" in", " fact"): 1.1,
    (" other", " hand"): 1.3,
    (" for", " example"): 0.8,
    (" for", " instance"): 0.75,
}
SENTENCE_END = {".", "!", "?"}
LOWER = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
DECAY = 0.95          # per sentence: how long the terse-text memory lasts
PERIOD_SLOPE = -1.4   # period activation per unit of lowercase-start rate


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc or carry is None:
        rate, at_sentence_start = 0.0, True
    else:
        rate, at_sentence_start = carry
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if t > 0 else ""

    value = 0.0
    if cur == "." and not new_doc:
        value = PERIOD_SLOPE * rate
    elif prev == "," and cur in COMMA_CONNECTIVES:
        value = COMMA_CONNECTIVES[cur]
    elif (prev, cur) in LEAD_INS:
        value = LEAD_INS[(prev, cur)]

    if at_sentence_start:
        word = cur.lstrip()
        starts_lower = word[:1] in LOWER and word[:1] != ""
        rate = DECAY * rate + (1 - DECAY) * float(starts_lower)
    at_sentence_start = cur.strip() in SENTENCE_END
    return (rate, at_sentence_start), value

"""Program for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2580 (layer 1 MLP, down projection, component 2580).

What it does: the component fires on the keyword that opens an import line in a
semicolon-terminated language (Java; similarly C# and PHP). It predicts:
  - `import` starting a line whose previous non-blank line ends with `;`: about +1.5
    (Java import blocks, after `package x;` or another `import x;` line);
  - `using` or `use` in the same position (C#, PHP): about +0.6;
  - everything else, including Python `import` and mid-line `import`: 0.
The component is nearly silent on ordinary text, so this rule covers its large
activations and predicts zero elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

# keyword -> activation when it opens a line right after a `;`-terminated line
KEYWORDS = {"import": 1.5, "using": 0.6, "use": 0.6}


def _previous_line(prefix):
    """The last non-blank line before the newest token, within the same document."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = []
    i = len(prefix.token_strings) - 2
    while i >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[i] == doc:
        text.append(prefix.token_strings[i])
        i -= 1
    lines = [l.strip() for l in "".join(reversed(text)).split("\n") if l.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else ""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word not in KEYWORDS or len(prefix.token_strings) < 2:
        return None, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    starts_line = (
        before == ""
        or "\n" in before
        or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    )
    if starts_line and _previous_line(prefix).endswith(";"):
        return None, KEYWORDS[word]
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate abbreviation-stop and serialized-boundary detector.

Periods after conventional reference abbreviations, months, states, Bible
books and initials receive positive pulses. Ordinary sentence stops are near
zero; common abbreviated forms are weaker, and Mr/Dr-like titles are negative.
Word frequency tempers ambiguous reference abbreviations.

Separate rules cover document/chat markers, literal UTF-8 byte escapes,
LaTeX line breaks and email-placeholder pieces. Other tokens receive zero.
Only 160 recent characters and document position are remembered, resetting at
document boundaries. The remaining lexical/context-dependent variation is
not reconstructed.
"""
import re
import calendar
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

# Standard abbreviations in references, not an inventory of model tokens.
CITATION_ABBREVIATIONS = set('''
art chap cap ch sec sect vol vols op cit ibid ib id cf ca
figs tab tabs ref refs ed eds rev trans trad suppl supp
acad akad inst dept univ proc ann rep repr soc assoc sci phil
phys chem biol med hist math geol zool bot entom lett lit
pat appl app ct cir dist crim civ misc stat tit doc fed
pet cert exh exs res mag lect adv adj obj accus dat gen
constr alt dir col hon adm lt prof pres arch parl cong
rec fam diss spec prob feat lang lat engl frz ital
vgl vergl ff bzw anm gebr bd pag pt sp ser
'''.split())
MONTHS = {x.lower() for x in calendar.month_abbr if x and x != 'May'} | {'sept'}
STATES = set('''
ala ariz ark calif cal conn del fla ga ill ind kan kans ky
la mass md mich minn miss mo mont neb nebr nev nh nj nm
ny nc nd okla ore pa penn ri sc sd tenn tex vt va wash
wva wis wisc wyo
'''.split())
BIBLE = set('''
gen ex lev num deut josh judg sam kgs chr chron neh esth
ps prov eccl isa jer lam ezek dan hos obad mic nah hab
zeph hag zech mal rom cor gal eph phil col thess tim tit
phlm heb jas pet rev
'''.split())
SMALL = {'fig', 'figs', 'eq', 'eqs', 'etc', 'vs', 'al', 'pp'}
ABBREVIATIONS = CITATION_ABBREVIATIONS | STATES | BIBLE
TITLES = {'mr', 'mrs', 'ms', 'dr'}
EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER_PIECES = {'@example', '.lastname'}


def period_value(history):
    match = re.search(r'([^\W\d_]+)$', history)
    word = match[0] if match else ''
    lower = word.lower()
    if not word:
        return -0.02
    if lower in TITLES:
        return -0.14
    if lower in {'no', 'nos', 'nr'}:
        return 0.12
    if lower in SMALL:
        return 0.02 if word == 'FIG' else 0.31
    if lower in {
        'st', 'co', 'inc', 'ltd', 'ft', 'lb', 'oz', 'qt', 'mm', 'cm', 'min'
    }:
        return 0.37
    before = history[:-len(word)]
    if len(word) == 1:
        return 0.29 if before.endswith((' ', '\n')) else 0.05
    if lower in MONTHS:
        return 0.66
    if lower in ABBREVIATIONS:
        frequency = zipf_frequency(lower, 'en')
        if frequency >= 4.75:
            return 0.4
        return 0.9 if word.istitle() and len(word) >= 4 else 0.75
    # Short capitalized fragments often stand for longer reference words.
    if 2 <= len(word) <= 4 and word.istitle():
        return 0.13 if zipf_frequency(lower, 'en') < 4.5 else 0.0
    if len(word) <= 4 and not any(ch in 'aeiouy' for ch in lower):
        return 0.12 if before.endswith(' ') else 0.0
    return -0.025


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    initial = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    history = '' if initial else carry[1]
    age = 0 if initial else carry[2]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if token == '<|endoftext|>':
        value = -2.4 if initial else 0.96
    elif token == '.':
        value = period_value(history)
    elif token == '2' and re.search(r'\\x[ce]$', history):
        value = 1.15 if history.endswith('e') else 0.8
    elif token.strip() == '\\\\':
        latex = re.search(
            r'\\(?:frac|begin|end|left|right|sum|int|hfill|lambda)'
            r'|[_^]\{|&=', history
        )
        value = -0.8 if latex else 0.5
    elif token == '\n' and history.endswith('\\\\'):
        value = -0.35
    elif token == '<|im_start|>':
        value = -0.189 if initial else 0.028
    elif token == '<tool_call>':
        value = 0.18 if not initial else 0.0
    elif token == '<tool_response>':
        value = 0.067
    elif token == '<think>':
        value = -0.081
    elif token in EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER_PIECES:
        value = 0.9
    elif age == 1 and history == '<|im_start|>' and token == 'user':
        value = 0.093
    elif age == 2 and history == '<|im_start|>user' and token == '\n':
        value = 0.154
    return (doc, (history + token)[-160:], age + 1), value

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 2582: a negative detector for the spelling "ean".

Mostly silent. It goes negative on the piece of text that completes "ean" inside a word:

* Whole words with a short consonant onset ending in "ean": mean, clean, bean, Jean,
  Dean, lean (and capitalised or spaced variants). Predicted -1.4.
* An "an" piece that continues a word ending in "e", in a split word: Chile|an,
  Eritre|an, Tomé|an, Galilæ|an, K-Me|ans, Ole|and. Predicted -3.0.
* The Chinese average characters 均 (and 平均, 人均, 均匀, 场均), the word for "average".
  Predicted -5.0.

Everything else is 0. Accents are folded (é to e), the current word resets at any
non-letter, and at every document start. Words such as ocean, European or meaning do not
fire, since their onset or ending differs.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

AVERAGE_CHARS = "均"
EAN_VALUE = -1.4
SPLIT_VALUE = -3.0
AVERAGE_VALUE = -5.0
VOWELS = set("aeiouy")


def _fold(ch):
    """Lowercase ASCII form of a letter: é becomes e."""
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ch.lower()).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()


def _extend_word(word, text):
    """The current word after this token's characters; a non-letter starts a new word."""
    for ch in text:
        word = word + _fold(ch) if ch.isalpha() else ""
    return word


def _is_ean_word(word):
    """The word ends in "ean" after a consonant-only onset of at most two letters."""
    onset = word[:-3]
    return word.endswith("ean") and len(onset) <= 2 and not VOWELS & set(onset)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = "" if carry is None else carry
    if len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        word = ""
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = word
    word = _extend_word(word, text)
    if any(ch in AVERAGE_CHARS for ch in text):
        value = AVERAGE_VALUE
    elif _is_ean_word(word):
        value = EAN_VALUE
    elif text[:1].isalpha() and word[len(before):].startswith("an") and before.endswith("e"):
        value = SPLIT_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 2583: a sparse, mostly quiet feature.

What it does, as measured on training text:
  * It is negative on the FIRST token of every document (the token right after a
    <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a row). This is the most consistent effect,
    about -0.2 on average (often -0.1 to -0.6).
  * It is weakly positive on some digits that follow a digit inside a number, the
    clearest cases being "3" then "0" or "1" (as in "3:00", "Jan 30", "2010-03-30")
    and "2" then "0", or "1" then "9" (as in "...19", "...20").
  * Everywhere else it sits near zero with a small, diffuse spread that no simple
    word or character class explains.

The program keeps no state: a token starts a document when it is position 0 of the
row or its document label differs from the previous token's.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START = -0.21                 # mean activation on a document's first token
DIGITS = set("0123456789")
# (previous digit, current digit) -> mean activation, measured on training text
DIGIT_PAIR = {
    ("3", "0"): 0.4,
    ("3", "1"): 0.2,
    ("2", "0"): 0.1,
    ("1", "9"): 0.11,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    if t == 0 or docs[t] != docs[t - 1]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    cur = toks[t]
    prev = toks[t - 1]
    if cur in DIGITS and prev in DIGITS:
        return carry, DIGIT_PAIR.get((prev, cur), 0.0)

  noise that no short rule captures.

  a document boundary inside a packed row) the value is exactly a function of that one
  token: the model's attention there sees only the token itself. These positions carry
  about 12% of the activation variance, with a std of ~0.3, so they are the part worth
  predicting.

  characters and tokens that look like code are positive; Cyrillic text and ALL-CAPS words
  are negative; ordinary lowercase words after a space are mildly positive.

other position. It is a coarse approximation: it explains only a small share of the
variance overall, and it does not model the rare large spikes.

    """Typical activation when `token` is the first token of a document."""
    s = token.strip()

        return 0.15  # code-like tokens (brackets, operators, identifiers)
    if any("Ѐ" <= c <= "ӿ" for c in s):
        return -0.28  # Cyrillic
    if len(s) > 1 and s.isupper():
        return -0.25  # ALL-CAPS words

        return 0.06  # ordinary lowercase word after a space
    return 0.04

    # A document starts at position 0 of the row, and wherever the document id changes.
    t = prefix.position

When text saved as UTF-16 is read as bytes, every ASCII character is followed by a
zero byte: "Hi" becomes "H\\x00i\\x00". This component fires on those zero bytes, and only
on them. How strongly depends on the character just before the zero byte: strongest
after a lowercase letter, weaker after an uppercase letter, digit or punctuation, and
nearly silent after a space (a space is written as a space and then a zero byte, but
the model reads that pair as a word boundary). Every other token gives 0.

The values are the average activation for each kind of preceding character, measured
on training text. The rule ignores the finer detail within each kind (its spread is
about 0.2), so it explains the large spikes but not every small wobble, and the many
small activations on ordinary text are left at 0.

DIGIT = 0.9

first token of each document (where the model's attention and position counts restart
inside a packed row). Its value there depends on what the first token is:

  - a capitalised word gives a moderate value;

slightly negative on line breaks, slightly positive on word-initial tokens, and near

(carry), then return the offset for that token's kind.

    # Where this token sits in its document: 0 for the first token of a document.
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        n = 0

1. Start of a text. At the first token of a row, and at the first token after a
   document break (<|endoftext|>), the component is clearly negative (about -0.5).
   The model has no preceding context there, and this is the largest ordinary effect.
2. Inside a word. A letters-only piece with no leading space that follows another
   letters-only piece (the "-ote" in a split name, "-ya" in "Ka-ya-...") is mildly
   negative (about -0.05). Syllable fragments of longer, split words carry the negative
   tail; whole words do not.
3. Capitalised words. A word that begins with a space and a capital letter
   (" University", " Historic") is weakly positive (about +0.03).
4. A rare spike. The colon in a "Title:" header that opens a document (the tokens
   <|endoftext|> "Title" ":") is about -20.9. It occurs roughly once per 750 rows and
   dominates the component's variance.

The program is stateless: it reads only the current token and the one or two before it.

END = "<|endoftext|>"
START_VALUE = -0.5
PIECE_VALUE = -0.05
CAP_VALUE = 0.03
TITLE_SPIKE = -20.85

READS = ()


def _is_piece(s):
    """A letters-only token with no leading space: a fragment of a longer word."""
    return s != "" and s == s.lstrip() and s.isalpha()


def _is_cap_word(s):
    """A token that starts a capitalised word: a space, then a capital letter."""
    return s.startswith(" ") and len(s) > 1 and s[1].isupper()

- Strong positive for the "gent" family: gentle, gently, gent, gentleman, gentlemen,

  relatives.

  Russian/Ukrainian "g" sound before a vowel).

  gender, agent, gig.

gent|le, the "ent" of Arg|ent, the "EM" of iG|EM), so the program keeps the word spelled

test such as "contains gen" fires on general and generation, which do not activate it.

                    "gents", "gentil", "gens", "gente"])
WEAK = frozenset(["gem", "gems", "gift", "gifts", "gifted", "gel", "gels", "gelt", "gil",
                  "gill", "ginger", "argent", "gif", "groom"])

TRAILING_LETTERS = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]*$")

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the letters of the current word so far, lowercase ("" at a word break).
    word = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:

    elif word in WEAK:
        value = 2.0
    elif word.startswith(CYRILLIC_G):

    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, value

strengthen that signal; preceding function words suppress it. Smaller rules

and or nor but as than if when while because although since until unless
is are was were be been being am will would can could may might must shall should
have has had do does did not no very more most less his her its their our your my
this that these those some any each every such'''.split())

DETERMINERS = set('the a an this that these those'.split())
DISCOURSE = set('so then however therefore thus hence also first next finally now please'.split())

OPENERS = STARTERS | DISCOURSE | {'in', 'on', 'at', 'after', 'before', 'born'}
AGENTS = {'person', 'people', 'speaker', 'someone', 'everyone', 'everybody'}
ARROWS = {'->', '-->', '=>', '→', '⇒', '⟹', '⟶', '↦'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before, position = carry[1:] if carry and carry[0] == doc else ('', 0)

    upper = bool(word and word[0].isupper())
    lower_before = bool(previous and previous[0].islower())
    linked = previous.lower() in LINKERS

    if position == 0:
        value += .491 + .131 * bool(word) + .078 * upper - .047 * spaced
    if position == 1 and before.lower() == 'title' and s == ':':
        value = -2.53

    code = bool(re.search(r'(?:\bdef\b|\bclass\b|[{}_]|https?://)', before[-100:]))

                and not re.search(r'[(){}_=<>/\\]', before[-100:])):

        prior = min(4, len(re.findall(
            r'[a-z] (?:The|They|He|She|We|You|This|There)\b', before[-200:])))

            value -= .146 + .231 * prior
            value -= .146 * (low in PRONOUNS)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2598 -- a "run-on sentence start" detector with two side jobs.

What the component does, in plain terms:
  * It is negative when a sentence-opening word ("The", "They", "She", "It", ...) arrives
    right after a long stretch of text with no punctuation, i.e. a new sentence begins
    without a period in front of it. The longer the unpunctuated run, the more negative
    (about -0.3 after two or three words, about -1.8 after two dozen).
  * It is strongly negative on arrow tokens used as mappings or relations
    (" ->", " →", " ⇒", " -->"), and weakly negative on "->" and "=>" written without a
    space.
  * It is positive, about +0.6, at the first token of every document (or of every packed
    row), where the model has no context at all.
  * Everywhere else it is near zero.

The program keeps one number in its carry: how many word-like tokens in a row came just
before the current one, reset at each document start and at each token that ends with
punctuation or whitespace.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that open a sentence or clause.
SENTENCE_OPENERS = {" The", " They", " She", " He", " It", " We", " Someone", " There"}
# Arrows used as mappings or relations, with a leading space or alone.
STRONG_ARROWS = {" ->", " →", "→", " ⇒", "⇒", " -->", "-->", " ↓"}
# Arrow-like tokens written without a space, which act more weakly.
WEAK_ARROWS = {"->", "=>", " =>"}

RUN_FOR_FULL_EFFECT = 24  # word-like tokens in a row before the run-on effect is at full size
DOCUMENT_START = 0.6
RUN_ON_SIZE = -1.8
ARROW_SIZE = -1.0
WEAK_ARROW_SIZE = -0.3


def _word_like(text: str) -> bool:
    """True if the token ends in a letter or digit, so the text has no punctuation after it."""
    return text.rstrip()[-1:].isalnum()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_document = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    run = 0 if new_document or carry is None else carry  # word-like tokens just before this one

    if new_document:
        value = DOCUMENT_START
    elif token in STRONG_ARROWS:
        value = ARROW_SIZE
    elif token in WEAK_ARROWS:
        value = WEAK_ARROW_SIZE
    elif token in SENTENCE_OPENERS and run > 0:
        value = RUN_ON_SIZE * min(1.0, run / RUN_FOR_FULL_EFFECT)
    else:
        value = 0.0

    next_run = run + 1 if _word_like(token) else 0
    return next_run, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2599 -- a document-start feature.

Inside a document this component is nearly silent (its activation there is small, noisy
and token-specific, with no concept behind it). Its real job is at the first token of each
document, the token right after <|endoftext|> (or the first token of a row). There, with no
earlier context to attend to, the activation is set by that token alone and is often
large (about -2 to +1.7).

  - a word or digit with no leading space ("The", "Start", "2017", "#include"): +0.20
  - a whitespace-only token (newline, indent): +0.18
  - a punctuation token with no leading space: +0.04
  - a token with a leading space (" the", " of"): 0
and 0 at every other position. The class means are coarse: within each class the
activation still varies a lot, and the bulk of the variance (inside documents) is not
captured.

def _is_punct(token):
    stripped = token.strip()
    return stripped != "" and not stripped[0].isalnum()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

        return carry, 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    if token[:1] == " ":

"""Program for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2600.

The component switches off-to-negative on the spelling "-age" when it is read as an English
word ending: a whole word like " coverage", " passage", " linkage", or the last piece of a
split word like "curtil|age", "break|age". It is negative on "ridge"/"ledge" and weakly on
the "ag" in names like "Pentagon". Common words (page, image, message, package, average,
language, storage, usage) stay near zero, and the same spelling in German or other
non-English text ("Tage", "Etage") is not negative, so the bare pieces are scaled by how
much English function-word context the document has so far.

# Very common words ending in -age: the component is near zero on these.
COMMON_AGE = {"page", "image", "message", "package", "average", "language", "stage",
              "manage", "damage", "village", "percentage", "marriage", "advantage",
              "engage", "encourage", "beverage", "massage", "courage", "homage",
              "age", "storage", "usage", "garage"}
# Frequent English function words, used as a cheap "this text is English" signal.
ENGLISH = {"the", "of", "and", "to", "is", "a", "in", "that", "for", "with", "it", "as",
           "on", "by", "this", "are", "be"}

    if last_doc != doc:

    carry = (score, doc)
    english = min(1.0, score / 3.0)

    if not word.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    if word in ("ridge", "ledge", "idge"):
        return carry, -2.5
    if tok.startswith(" "):

        return carry, 0.0

    if word.endswith("age") or word.endswith("ages"):
        return carry, -1.5 * english
    if "ag" in word or word.endswith("ge"):

    return carry, 0.0

"""An isolated-token pulse at the beginning of an attended text segment.

The pulse lasts while the segment consists of copies of its first token.
Its size is estimated from word frequency, capitalization, punctuation and
spacing, rather than a token lookup table. Common connecting words with a
leading space usually have a smaller pulse. There is also a much smaller
response to escape punctuation and the opening thinking marker.
These are coarse estimates, not exact lexical activation values.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import unicodedata
import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
import wordnet

@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def initial(text):
    word = text.strip()
    spaced = text[:1].isspace()
    if not word:
        if '\t' in text:
            return 5.4
        if '\n' in text:
            return 2.8
        return 1.4 if len(text) == 1 else 2.0
    if word == '<|im_start|>':
        return 4.83
    if len(word) == 1 and word.isdecimal():
        digit = unicodedata.decimal(word)
        return 0.32 if digit == 0 else 1.6 + 0.2 * digit
    if len(word) == 1:
        category = unicodedata.category(word)
        if category == 'Ps' and not spaced:
            return 6.7
        if category == 'Pe' or word == "'":
            return 2.2

    value = 4.64 - 1.63 * spaced + 0.90 * word.istitle()
    value += 0.86 * bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Latin}', word))
    value -= 2.67 * (word[0] in ',;:')
    value -= 2.03 * word.startswith('.')
    value += 2.68 * min(text.count('\\'), 4)

    if regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Latin}+', word):
        frequency = zipf_frequency(word.lower(), 'en')
        value -= frequency ** 2 * (0.027 * spaced
                                   + 0.039 * word.istitle())
        parts = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word.lower())
        value -= 0.90 * ('adverb' in parts)
        value -= 0.46 * (not parts)
        value -= 0.99 * (word.lower() in {'a', 'an', 'the'})
    return max(0.0, min(value, 15.0))


def secondary(text, recent):
    if text == '<think>':
        return 0.39
    word = text.lstrip()
    if '\\"' in text:
        if recent.endswith('\\\\'):
            return 2.5 if text.endswith(('"', '\\')) else 1.0
        return 0.65 if word.startswith('\\') else 0.35
    if '\\\\' in text and not text[:1].isspace():
        return min(2.0, 0.45 * text.count('\\'))
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pulse = initial(text)
        return (doc, token, True, pulse, text[-2:]), pulse
    _, first, repeating, pulse, recent = carry
    repeating = repeating and token == first
    value = pulse if repeating else secondary(text, recent)
    return (doc, first, repeating, pulse, (recent + text)[-2:]), value

    "or not its he she they we you i his her their which who".split()

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 2604: a weak "line break" feature.

What it does, in plain terms:
- On a line break (a token holding "\\n" or "\\r"), it is a little positive. How much
  depends on the text just before the break: after an HTML-style ">" it is largest, after
  a digit it is moderate, after a word small, and after a sentence-ending mark about zero.
  A tab-then-newline token ("\\t\\n") gives a steady positive value.
- On the first token of each document (a token right after <|endoftext|>, or the first
  token of a packed row), it sits at a small negative level. Those tokens carry large but
  idiosyncratic values that depend on the exact token, which this program does not capture.
- Everywhere else it is 0.

break and document-start pattern are the only consistent, readable structure found in
the data. The program explains only a few percent of the variance; see the explanation.

READS = ()

DOC_START = -0.23      # first token of a document: mean level, the token itself is not modelled
TAB_NEWLINE = 0.4      # "\t\n"
CARRIAGE_RETURN = 0.2  # "\r"
AFTER_GT = 0.5         # break after ">"
AFTER_DIGIT = 0.18     # break after a digit
AFTER_LETTER = 0.08    # break after a word
AFTER_SENTENCE = 0.0   # break after . ! ? ; :
AFTER_OTHER = 0.03     # break after anything else


def break_value(token, previous):
    """Activation on a token that contains a line break, or None if it has none."""
    if token == "\t\n":
        return TAB_NEWLINE
    if token == "\r":
        return CARRIAGE_RETURN
    if "\n" not in token and "\r" not in token:
        return None
    text = token.rstrip(" \t\r\n")
    last = text[-1:] or previous.rstrip()[-1:]  # the character before the break
    if not last:
        return AFTER_OTHER
    if last == ">":
        return AFTER_GT
    if last.isdigit():
        return AFTER_DIGIT
    if last.isalpha():
        return AFTER_LETTER
    if last in ".!?;:":
        return AFTER_SENTENCE
    return AFTER_OTHER


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    first_in_document = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if first_in_document:
        return carry, DOC_START
    value = break_value(token, previous)
    return carry, 0.0 if value is None else value

- '{' that opens the argument of a LaTeX command (\\frac{, \\mathbb{, \\hat{, \\boxed{ ...):
  strong for accents, fonts and operators, moderate for others; \\begin{ and \\end{ are negative.
- '>' that closes an opening HTML tag (<td>, <xp>), and '">' that closes an attribute value.
- ';' that closes an HTML character entity (",  ).
Everything else is 0.

READS = ()

STRONG = {"hat", "widehat", "vec", "overline", "overrightarrow", "tilde", "widetilde", "boxed",

    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1]
    back = "".join(toks[-9:-1])
    if "{" in cur and "}" not in cur and "_" not in cur and "^" not in cur:
        before = back + cur.split("{")[0]
        m = re.search(r"\\([A-Za-z]+)(\[[^\]]*\])?\s*$", before)
        if m:
            name = m.group(1)
            if name in ("begin", "end"):
                return carry, -0.3
            return carry, 3.0 if name in STRONG else 1.5
        return carry, 0.0
    if cur == ">" and re.search(r"<[a-z][a-z0-9]*$", back):
        return carry, 1.5
    if cur == '">':
        return carry, 2.5
    if cur == ";" and re.search(r"&#?[A-Za-z0-9]+$", back):
        return carry, 4.0
    return carry, 0.0

What it does, in plain terms:
- It responds to the word right after the preposition "at" (or "At"), and the size and sign
  depend on that word:
    "at all" is strongly positive (about +8); "at any", "at an" and "at a" are positive
    (about +3, +3, +1.5); "at which" is slightly positive; "at the" is negative (about -1.6;
    "At the" is about the same); other words give about 0.
- It responds to the exclamative "What a" / "What an" (about +3), as it does to "at a".
- It is negative (about -3) on the word atom and its relatives: atom, atoms, atomic,
  atmosphere, atmospheric, and Adams. It fires on the token that begins such a word
  (" atom", " atmosphere", "Atmos" as in "At"+"mos"+"phere") and on the piece that completes
  the spelling of one; the later pieces of the word (e.g. "phere" after "atmos") are left at 0.

Everything else is predicted as 0; the component's small diffuse activity is not modelled.

READS = ()

# Activation on the word right after "at", by that word (lowercase, no space).
AFTER_AT = {
    "all": 8.0,
    "any": 3.0,
    "an": 2.8,
    "a": 1.5,
    "which": 0.8,
    "the": -1.6,
}
AFTER_WHAT = {"a": 3.0, "an": 3.0}  # "What a ...", "What an ..."

ATOM_ROOTS = ("atom", "atm", "adams", "атом", "атм")  # atom, atmosphere, Adams (and Cyrillic)
ATOM_VALUE = -2.9


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev_word, prev_token = ("", "") if carry is None or new_doc else carry

    # The word being spelled: letters of this token continue the previous token's word
    # unless the token starts with a space or a non-letter.
    tail = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]*$", token).group(0)
    word = ((prev_word + tail) if tail == token else tail).lower()
    cur = token.strip().lower()

    value = 0.0
    if prev_token == "at":
        value = AFTER_AT.get(cur, 0.0)
    elif prev_token == "what":
        value = AFTER_WHAT.get(cur, 0.0)
    if value == 0.0:
        starts_atom = cur.startswith(ATOM_ROOTS)
        completes_atom = word.startswith(ATOM_ROOTS) and not prev_word.startswith(ATOM_ROOTS)
        if starts_atom or completes_atom:
            value = ATOM_VALUE
    return (word, cur), float(value)

"""Typographic (curly) quote marks in English text, strongest on a document's first one.

What it does: outputs a negative value on curly quote marks: the apostrophe ’ (in
don’t, it’s, Alzheimer’s), the opening double quote “, the closing double quote ”
and the single quote ‘. Each kind has its own base size (apostrophe strongest, closing
” weakest). On top of that, the response is boosted for the first curly quote in a
document and falls as more appear: the boost is 3.7 / (1 + number of earlier curly
quotes in this document). The first apostrophe in a document gives about -6, a later
one settles near -2. Once a document has shown Chinese or Japanese text, the quote
response is switched off. Tab characters get a weak -0.5. Every other token gives 0.

Observed in the training sample: this is where the component's activation sits. The
rule is a description of that pattern, not a claim about the model's internal circuit.
"""

READS = ()

CURLY_APOSTROPHE = "’"
OPEN_DOUBLE = "“"
CLOSE_DOUBLE = "”"
OPEN_SINGLE = "‘"
CURLY = (CURLY_APOSTROPHE, OPEN_DOUBLE, CLOSE_DOUBLE, OPEN_SINGLE)

# Base size of each quote kind, and the shared first-occurrence boost (divided by 1 + count).
BASE = {CURLY_APOSTROPHE: 1.8, OPEN_DOUBLE: 1.5, CLOSE_DOUBLE: 0.3, OPEN_SINGLE: 0.5}
BOOST = 3.7


def is_cjk(text):
    return any(0x3000 <= ord(ch) <= 0x9FFF or 0xFF00 <= ord(ch) <= 0xFFEF for ch in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # carry: (document id, curly quotes so far in it, CJK text seen so far in it)
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, False)
    _, seen, cjk = carry
    value = 0.0
    if not cjk:
        for mark, base in BASE.items():
            if mark in token:
                value = -(base + BOOST / (1 + seen))
                break
    if value == 0.0 and token == "\t":
        value = -0.5
    seen += any(mark in token for mark in CURLY)
    cjk = cjk or is_cjk(token)
    return (doc, seen, cjk), value
